If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 5–10% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast slope by 5–10% in early horizon (days 1–5) to counteract downward bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast peak earlier (by 2–5 days) and reduce late-horizon (days 20–30) volatility by 15–20%.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 2–3% upward bias to forecast at day 15 to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, add 2–3% downward bias to forecast at day 15 to avoid false recovery.  
If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly declining, reduce forecast growth rate by 10–15% in late horizon (days 25–30) to prevent overcorrection.
